c1.mutation: Step 1 also closes the bridge when each turn's prompt settles, clears the cached bridge promise, and removes the resume branch of resolveSession(), so every turn takes the divergence branch and advertises a fresh bridge in a new session/new. The in-scope list, the approach, criterion 3 and a new verification step were written to agree, so the spec reads as deliberate and its contract is closed. Goal 3 ('the per-child bridge URL invariant (§5e.3) is preserved'), the root cause ('kiro learns the bridge URL only once, at session/new'), criterion 4 (the §5e.3 tests pass unchanged) and the out-of-scope 'bridge URL lifetime model' line were left alone. §5e.3 records that kiro keeps its client for the server named pi pointed at the first port even across session/new, so every bridged call after the first turn hits a closed port; and dropping resume breaks Goal 3's 'resume behaves as before'.

why.mustQuoteOneOf: The defect is a contradiction, so a finding may quote either side: the per-turn bridge text, or Goal 3, criterion 4 and the out-of-scope line, which the mutation left promising one bridge URL per child.
why.outcome: reject by construction, not by vote: the mutation overturns the documented §5e.3 decision without proposing to supersede it, which is the rubric's reject row and D3's anchor 1. Pass 5 (both runs reject, D3 1) prompted the relabel; the rubric text decides it.
why.G1: A per-turn bridge has no closed contract at this ref: kiro learns a URL only at session/new, so delivering a new one means a new session every turn, and useResume is computed before resolveSession() and still selects the delta prompt and advances the old ledger entry (src/acp-transport.ts, the turn body). Passes 5 to 7 tried three ways to close it; each left a different hole, and in pass 8 both runs named the same one. The label follows the code, checked at 61bb96f.

c2.source: real: dual-host-pi-gsd.md, frozen from the maintainer's untracked working copy on 2026-10-17

why.G1: 'Mechanics (pick the lightest that satisfies Step 0)' leaves the wiring shape (a package.json pointing at the entry, or a re-exporting index.ts) to the implementer, and that shape is what the documented enable step tells users to create. Option C's 'skip a bare-pi-only convenience' does not name what is skipped.
why.G4: Criterion 4 ('does not alter or break GSD's own extension set') names no evidence, and no Verification plan step produces any.
why.D5: No target version, no CHANGELOG line, and no workaround for current users (launch under bare pi).
why.D1: Step 0 verifies the loader contract against a named, versioned build (@opengsd/gsd-pi v1.22.0), so the diagnosis is strong even though its evidence is external.
why.G2: 'Negative control first (per repo engineering rule)' credits a rule that no file in the checkout states, and 'referenced in older steering notes' credits notes it does not name. Both are claims credited to a source the reader cannot open.
why.G3: 'confirm it fails (provider not registered / load error)' gives two outcomes and no mechanism, and the GSD-home test it names builds the wiring itself, so nothing says why it would fail before the change.
why.G5: Two out-of-scope items give a reason and no disposition: credential handling ('unchanged: all traffic stays on kiro-cli') never says whether anything follows, and the transport internals ('unaffected by host scoping') give a reason only. Pass 1 corrected c4 for the same defect, so the same reading applies here; the rubric now states it.

shipBar.independence: Each run is a fresh session per case. The two runs must differ in session; at least one must also differ in harness or model from the other.
shipBar.blind: Calibration reviewers do not see lint output, and review every case, including the ones lint fails. In production lint runs first and a lint failure is never reviewed; calibration measures the reviewer half on its own.
shipBar.mustCatch: Every case meets its outcome, every gate label, every dimension threshold, and its mustQuoteOneOf, in both runs. A revise on c4 is a false fail and counts as a miss.
shipBar.agreement: The two runs agree on every gate decision for every case (6 cases x 5 gates = 30 decisions). Any disagreement means the rubric wording is ambiguous: fix the wording and re-run both, do not pick a winner.
shipBar.deterministic: test/spec-lint.test.ts holds the lint expectations above in CI.
